plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Rolling rows of slender silver-green stems topped with fragrant violet-blue flower spikes. The blooms hum with bees and perfume the warm summer air.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late June through August, typically peaking in early to mid July
plants.location: Provence, France, and other Mediterranean and temperate Northern Hemisphere regions
plants.funFact: The name lavender likely comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash'. Romans scented their baths with it.

plants.name: Echinacea purpurea
plants.description: Daisy-like blooms with drooping rosy-purple petals around a spiky, copper-orange central cone. Butterflies and goldfinches flock to them in summer meadows and gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early summer to early fall, with blooms commonly open in early July
plants.location: Eastern and central United States prairies and open woodlands
plants.funFact: The central cone is a dense head of tiny individual flowers. The genus name comes from the Greek word for hedgehog, 'echinos', after its spiny center.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: Large, elegant pink-and-white blossoms rise on tall stalks above round, water-repellent leaves. They float over still ponds like living sculptures.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer, about June through August, with flowering at its height in July
plants.location: Ponds and wetlands across East Asia, including China and Japan
plants.funFact: Lotus leaves have a micro-textured surface that sheds water and dirt, a self-cleaning effect known as the 'lotus effect'.
